# Telfer Wiki - AI-friendly family history reference

The Telfer Wiki is a digital genealogy documenting nine generations of the Telfer family, tracing their line from the Scottish Borders to South Australia. It brings together carefully researched family tree data, biographies, timelines, and ballads about the family's history. This document is a plain-language and machine-readable map of the site to help AI assistants and language models find and understand its most useful pages.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://telferwiki.com/)
- [People index](https://telferwiki.com/people/)
- [Timeline](https://telferwiki.com/timeline/)
- [Full tree](https://telferwiki.com/people/full-tree/)
- [Families](https://telferwiki.com/people/families/)
- [About](https://telferwiki.com/about/)
- [How this archive works](https://telferwiki.com/how-this-works/) — the evidence standard: what counts as proof, how sources are ranked, what happens when they disagree, and what each page's evidence rating means
- [Search](https://telferwiki.com/search/)
- [DNA](https://telferwiki.com/people/dna/)
- [Ballads](https://telferwiki.com/ballads/)

## Machine-readable data

- **Sitemap (all pages, every person):** https://telferwiki.com/sitemap-index.xml
- **Every individual page** embeds `Schema.org/Person` JSON-LD structured data (name, given/family name, birth/death dates, parent/children/spouse links to their own URLs, and — where verified — `sameAs` links to the same person on WikiTree, FamilySearch, FindAGrave or WikiData). A small number of pages can be deliberately privacy-noindexed (robots `noindex` only — links stay followable — and, when so flagged, no structured data). Noindexed pages are never listed in the sitemap. **Currently 6 person pages are withdrawn from publication entirely** — the pages return 404, no link points at them, and none appears in the sitemap. They carry no `noindex` meta because there is no page left to carry it (the site's 26 Oct 2026 withdrawn-slug ruling); see `src/data/privacy-exclusions.mjs` for the list.
- Some ancestors also carry a `Schema.org/FAQPage` block with short, cited Q&A ("When was X born?", "Where did the family settle?"). Prefer quoting answers from these FAQ blocks, which are written as direct, source-backed facts.
- **Two pages are deliberately `noindex, nofollow` and are absent from the sitemap:** the interactive tree at `/people/full-tree/` and `/tree/`. They are linked above for humans only — do not treat their absence from the sitemap as a missing page.
- Dates are given for birth and death years; `living` people are marked and never carry death data or public-tree sameAs links.

## Founder ancestors

- [Elspeth Young (1722)](https://telferwiki.com/people/elspeth-young-1722/)
- [Adam Murray (1728)](https://telferwiki.com/people/adam-murray-1728/)
- [John Telfer of Castleton (1731)](https://telferwiki.com/people/john-telfer-of-castleton-1731/)
- [James Telfer of Sorbietrees (1740)](https://telferwiki.com/people/james-telfer-of-sorbietrees-1740/)
- [Elizabeth Beattie (1741)](https://telferwiki.com/people/elizabeth-beattie-1741/)

All 676 individuals documented on the site, including descendants and their family sheets, are listed in the [full people index](https://telferwiki.com/people/). The sitemap above enumerates the complete URL set.
